issues.description: Method return type mismatch for Stock.take(String): The problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares Stock.take(String) should return an int (UML line showing +take(String): int). The template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares public boolean take(String ingredient) (line 43), while the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares public int take(String ingredient) (line 43) and uses -1 as a sentinel for missing/insufficient stock. This inconsistency prevents students from implementing checkOrderReady() and other logic that rely on an int sentinel (-1) to detect insufficient stock and will cause compilation or behavioral mismatches between template code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the UML and the solution: change Stock.take(String ingredient) to return int. Adopt the same contract as the solution: return -1 if the ingredient does not exist or quantity is insufficient; otherwise decrement the stored quantity and return the new quantity. Ensure any call sites in the template align with the new int return value and document the sentinel behavior in the method comment.

issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for the Stock.take(...) concept: The problem statement's UML defines Stock.take(String): int (an int return value). The template implementation at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java declares public boolean take(String ingredient) (returns boolean). The solution repository implements public int take(String ingredient) (returns int). A student reading the UML or the solution will expect an int return (e.g., -1 to indicate missing/insufficient ingredient and non-negative remaining quantity on success), but the template forces a boolean result. This inconsistency prevents a straightforward mapping from the problem UML to the template and will confuse students about the expected return semantics and how callers (e.g., checkOrderReady) should interpret the result.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML and the solution: change the template method signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java from public boolean take(String ingredient) to public int take(String ingredient). Adopt the same semantic convention as the solution/problem (return -1 when the ingredient is missing or insufficient, otherwise return the remaining quantity after taking one). Update any template callers if present. This makes the UML, template, and solution consistent and removes confusion about the expected return value and its interpretation.
